thread: Is the sacred in the act rather than the belief?
summary: Each piece asks whether doing the holy thing can matter more than believing in it. Xunzi argues it: the funeral and sacrifice rites are, in his account, a way of giving grief its proper form, and the wise treat them as human practice while ordinary people take them as the work of spirits, with both groups doing the same act. Larkin images it: a man with no faith keeps stopping at empty churches and finds he cannot say why the place still holds him. Peretz dramatises it: the sceptic follows the Rebbe to prove he never goes to heaven, sees only a woodcutter's errand, and still ends up a believer. Nick Cave sings around it: a singer who says he does not believe in an intervening God and still turns every line into a prayer for the person he loves.

pieces.essay: Xunzi argues it: ritual is justified by what it does for the living, whether or not anyone is listening.
pieces.poem: Larkin images it: an unbeliever in an empty church, still unable to treat it as just a building.
pieces.story: Peretz dramatises it: the proof of devotion is a bundle of firewood, and the sceptic accepts it as the same thing as heaven.
pieces.song: Cave sings around it: disbelief and prayer in the same breath, held together by the one being addressed.

forYou: The pontianak rites and spirit-appeasing customs in When Jasmine Blooms are the same question for a modern audience: what the ritual does for the people performing it when the thing it addresses may not be there.
